claims.claim: MasTec is a build-and-maintain bridge between capital, skilled field labor/electrical capability and physical communications, power, pipeline, clean-energy and data-center infrastructure; Q2 2026 backlog of $21.4B and Superior's data-center electrical capability broaden exposure to grid and compute buildout.

factors.name: alignment2036
factors.basis: Core work directly expands and maintains power, communications and other critical infrastructure.

factors.name: crossDivisionLeverage
factors.basis: Superior adds data-center electrical capability to existing power-delivery and infrastructure construction, enabling broader customer solutions.

factors.name: bottleneckControl
factors.basis: Scale, skilled labor, safety/execution systems and customer relationships matter, but construction services remain competitively contestable and project-specific.

factors.name: scenarioRobustness
factors.basis: Four infrastructure segments diversify end-market exposure, though each remains capital-cycle and project-timing sensitive.

risks.risk: Demand exposure is strong but economic capture depends on project selection, labor productivity, working capital and integration execution.

unknowns.unknown: Exact data-center share of consolidated backlog remains unquantified.

claims.claim: Q2 operating momentum and backlog are strong, but free cash flow was negative $59M and the $1.6B Superior acquisition used about $1.2B cash plus shares and an earn-out, creating a concrete integration/capital-allocation test.

factors.name: financialOperatingMomentum
factors.basis: Revenue, earnings and EBITDA expanded materially while quarterly free cash flow remained negative.

factors.name: governancePower
factors.basis: Superior expands capability but increases integration, purchase-price and earn-out execution risk.

risks.risk: Backlog can mislead if project mix, change orders, delays or execution costs compress realized margins.
Superior integration and acquisition financing can dilute expected strategic benefits if synergies or cash conversion disappoint.
Infrastructure spending is exposed to customer capital budgets, permitting, rates and labor availability.

contradictions.claim: Record earnings/backlog coexist with negative quarterly free cash flow.
contradictions.resolution: Retain both; strong demand/execution is supported, but cash conversion remains an explicit present weakness to monitor rather than a blocker.

unknowns.unknown: Post-close Superior standalone margin and cash conversion are not yet observable.
